_about: The harnesses the tracker follows: the agent software around a model that turns it into a working agent. Adoption and release data are collected automatically by pipeline/fetch_harnesses.py; this list is editorial.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.pricing: Subscription (Pro $20/mo, Max from $100/mo; not on Free) or pay-per-token API key / Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry
harnesses.notes: Public GitHub repo holds docs, plugins, changelog and issues, not the source; LICENSE.md reads 'All rights reserved' under Anthropic's Commercial Terms. Works only with Claude models (direct, or via Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry); the docs state routing to non-Claude models through gateways is not supported.

facts.pricing: Subscription (Pro $20/mo, Max from $100/mo; not on Free) or pay-per-token API key / Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry
open_questions: launch uses first npm publish (0.2.6, 2025-02-24, research preview); GA came later (May 2025) — pick which date the site means by 'launch'.
Metrics telemetry is on by default only for the direct Claude API; off by default on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry.

harnesses.repo_note: docs and issues repository (source is closed)
harnesses.downloads_partial: most installs now use Anthropic's native installer, which npm does not count

harnesses.name: OpenAI Codex
harnesses.pricing: Included in ChatGPT plans (Free, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo, Business, Enterprise) or API key at API prices
harnesses.notes: The CLI/agent core is Apache-2.0; the VS Code extension and desktop app ship under separate licence terms. Defaults to OpenAI models but documents --oss for Ollama/LM Studio and arbitrary custom model_providers (e.g. Mistral, proxies).
aka: OpenAI Codex (CLI, IDE extension, app, cloud)

facts.pricing: Included in ChatGPT plans (Free, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo, Business, Enterprise) or API key at API prices
open_questions: models classified 'any' because arbitrary providers are officially configurable; OpenAI remains the default and some features (cloud tasks, Slack) need a ChatGPT plan — 'own-plus' is defensible.
developers.openai.com/codex docs now 308-redirect to learn.chatgpt.com/docs; website field may need updating.
Telemetry: anonymous usage/health metrics on by default, disabled with [analytics] enabled=false; OTel export is opt-in.

harnesses.name: Cursor
harnesses.pricing: Free tier; Plus $8/mo (Grok models only); Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200/mo; Teams $30+/user; third-party models billed at API list price
harnesses.notes: SpaceX completed its all-stock acquisition of Anysphere (implied $60B) on 2026-08-14; plans are now bundled with Grok and X features, and only Grok/Composer models are in the included usage pool, with Claude, GPT, Gemini and others billed at API list price (Premium and up). VS Code fork; the public cursor/cursor repo holds only a README and security policy.

facts.pricing: Free tier; Plus $8/mo (Grok models only); Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200/mo; Teams $30+/user; third-party models billed at API list price
open_questions: launch '2023-03' rests on the public cursor/cursor repo creation date (2023-03-12) plus secondary profiles; no primary launch post found.

models: BYOK limited to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock (chat only); docs do not mention custom base URLs or local models — 'own-plus' vs 'curated' is a judgement call now that Grok is the default.
Telemetry: data-use page only describes Privacy Mode (training/retention), nothing on client telemetry or whether it can be disabled.
Whether 'web' (cloud agents) and Slack/'Grok Bot' should count as interfaces; only CLI confirmed from docs.
cursor/cursor repo is empty apart from README/SECURITY; stars are a weak adoption signal.

harnesses.name: GitHub Copilot
harnesses.pricing: Free tier (2,000 completions + 50 chat requests/mo); Pro $10/mo, Pro+ $39/mo, Max $100/mo; Business/Enterprise via sales; BYOK possible
harnesses.notes: Copilot CLI ships under a custom GitHub licence that forbids modification (repo holds only README, changelog, installer); the VS Code Copilot Chat client was MIT-licensed and in 2026 moved into the main microsoft/vscode repo. Both CLI and VS Code support BYOK, including OpenAI-compatible local endpoints such as Ollama and vLLM.

facts.pricing: Free tier (2,000 completions + 50 chat requests/mo); Pro $10/mo, Pro+ $39/mo, Max $100/mo; Business/Enterprise via sales; BYOK possible
open_questions: source: CLI is proprietary but the VS Code chat client is MIT (now inside microsoft/vscode) — 'open-core' could be argued; we used the CLI licence.

Telemetry: CLI's COPILOT_OFFLINE=true is documented to stop contact with GitHub servers (implying default-on telemetry); VS Code side follows telemetry.telemetryLevel. No single page states the default explicitly.
Not on Open VSX (GitHub.copilot / GitHub.copilot-chat not found there).
Launch = Copilot technical preview 2021-06-29 (marketplace release date); Copilot CLI npm package first published 2025-09-25.
Plans page did not show Business/Enterprise prices.

harnesses.name: Gemini CLI
harnesses.pricing: Paid Gemini API / Vertex AI keys or Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences; individual free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended 2026-06-18 (moved to Antigravity CLI)
harnesses.notes: Google announced on 2026-05-19 that Gemini CLI is being folded into the Go-based Antigravity CLI; since 2026-06-18 it no longer serves free, Google AI Pro/Ultra or individual Code Assist users, only enterprise licences and paid API keys. The Apache-2.0 repo is still active (releases in Oct 2026); the README still advertises the old free tier.

facts.pricing: Paid Gemini API / Vertex AI keys or Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences; individual free and Google AI Pro/Ultra access ended 2026-06-18 (moved to Antigravity CLI)
open_questions: Status kept 'active' because the repo and npm releases continue and enterprise/API-key users are served; for individuals it is effectively replaced by Antigravity CLI (proprietary per press reports, licence not verified) — consider a separate Antigravity CLI entry.
Quota page still lists free tiers (1,000 req/day Google account, 250/day unpaid key) alongside the replacement notice; unclear which free paths still work.
Experimental Gemma router can call a local LiteRT-LM endpoint, but only as a router alongside Gemini, so local_models=false.

harnesses.name: opencode
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional OpenCode Zen pay-as-you-go models and OpenCode Go subscription ($10/mo, Go Plus $40/mo)
harnesses.notes: Repo moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode (GitHub redirects); the docs footer credits Anomaly. Not the same project as the original Go 'opencode' (opencode-ai/opencode), which is archived and continued as Charm's Crush.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional OpenCode Zen pay-as-you-go models and OpenCode Go subscription ($10/mo, Go Plus $40/mo)
open_questions: Telemetry: no telemetry statement found in the docs; the CLI shows no product analytics in code search, but the desktop app initialises Sentry error reporting when built with a DSN (packages/desktop/src/renderer/startup/sentry.ts). Left null.
Launch date is the first GitHub release (0.0.45, 2025-05-14); the wider public launch announcement may be later (npm opencode-ai first published 2025-05-31).

harnesses.name: OpenClaw
harnesses.pricing: Free; no paid tier or hosted service (you pay your model provider)
harnesses.notes: Personal assistant agent that runs on your machine and is used through WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, iMessage and about 25 other chat channels. Formerly Warelay, Clawdbot and Moltbot (renamed to OpenClaw on 2026-01-30). Created by Peter Steinberger (now at OpenAI), it is stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation, a 501(c)(3); OpenAI is a donor, not an owner. It builds on Pi's components. A daily version check is on by default; feature statistics are opt-in.

facts.pricing: Free; no paid tier or hosted service (you pay your model provider)
open_questions: Interfaces 'tui' and 'web' are based on the existence of docs pages docs.openclaw.ai/tui and docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui (the gateway's browser Control UI). I did not read them in full.
Telemetry is 'opt-in' for usage statistics, but a daily update check (version/OS in User-Agent, Cloudflare-derived location) is on by default. You could also describe that as 'on, opt-out'.
OpenClaw Enterprise (an MIT control plane, announced 2026-09-29) is a separate project and is not covered here.

harnesses.name: Hermes Agent
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional Nous Portal subscription (Plus $20/mo, Super $100/mo, Ultra $200/mo)
harnesses.notes: Persistent self-improving agent: it writes and refines its own skills and keeps memory across sessions. It is used from a terminal UI or from Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and email through one gateway, and can run on a VPS or serverless backends. Sharing metrics with Nous takes two separate opt-ins (collect, then send).

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional Nous Portal subscription (Plus $20/mo, Super $100/mo, Ultra $200/mo)
open_questions: Exact launch day not found in a primary source. The v0.2.0 release notes (2026-03-12) say the project went public 'just over two weeks' earlier, which fits the 2026-02-25 date reported by secondary sources.
PyPI package first published only 2026-05-14 (install is mainly via script), so PyPI download counts understate usage.
There is an ACP adapter (acp_adapter/) for editor integration; 'ide-extension' was not added because I found no official extension.
GitHub releases carry no binary assets, so github_release_downloads=false.

harnesses.downloads_partial: the official installer clones the code from GitHub; only the side channel on PyPI is counted

harnesses.name: pi
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key or log in with a provider subscription
harnesses.notes: A minimal, extensible coding-agent harness by Mario Zechner. It deliberately leaves out sub-agents and plan mode and is extended through packages, with an SDK and an RPC mode. Earendil (Armin Ronacher's company) acquired it on 2026-04-08, Zechner joined Earendil, and the repo moved from badlogic/pi-mono to earendil-works/pi. Pi 1.0 shipped 2026-10-01.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key or log in with a provider subscription
open_questions: Status could also be 'acquired:Earendil' (acquired 2026-04-08, still actively developed). I used 'active' and named Earendil as vendor.
Launch = first npm publish of @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent (2025-11-12, at version 0.6.2), so there may have been earlier releases. The pi-mono repo was created 2025-08-09.
Telemetry: enableInstallTelemetry defaults to true (anonymous install/update reports and provider attribution headers); enableAnalytics is opt-in and off.
npm downloads are split: old package @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent (deprecated) and new @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (from 2026-05-07). Sum both for history.

harnesses.name: Kilo Code
harnesses.pricing: Free with your own key or local models; Kilo Gateway credits at provider rates, Kilo Pass ($19-$199/mo), Teams $15/user/mo, Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Started in 2025 as a fork of Roo Code/Cline (Apache-2.0). The current products are rebuilt on a fork of OpenCode (MIT): the Kilo CLI is an OpenCode fork, and the old codebase now sits archived in Kilo-Org/kilocode-legacy. So the main repo's licence went from Apache-2.0 to MIT. Available for VS Code, JetBrains, CLI and as a cloud agent.

facts.pricing: Free with your own key or local models; Kilo Gateway credits at provider rates, Kilo Pass ($19-$199/mo), Teams $15/user/mo, Enterprise custom
open_questions: Launch = VS Code Marketplace first publish (2025-03-07); the repo was created 2025-03-10.
'tui' assumed because the Kilo CLI is an OpenCode fork (OpenCode has a TUI); not separately confirmed in Kilo docs.

harnesses.name: Cline
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key (pay only for inference); Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Began as 'Claude Dev' (the extension id still says so) and now ships as a VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, CLI, desktop app and SDK. The JetBrains plugin is not open source. Telemetry is on by default across all clients, and one shared switch turns it off.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key (pay only for inference); Enterprise custom
open_questions: npm package 'cline' existed since 2013 under another owner; Cline's own versions start 2025-10-13 (1.0.0-nightly). Old download history is not Cline's.
ClinePass (a Cline-hosted inference offering referenced in the telemetry docs) exists, but I could not find its price; the pricing page lists no figure.
Whether the closed JetBrains plugin makes it 'open-core' is a judgement call; it is free, so I kept 'open-source'.

harnesses.name: OpenHands
harnesses.pricing: Free self-hosted (bring your own key); OpenHands Cloud individual tier free with BYOK or at-cost LLM usage; Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Started as OpenDevin in March 2024. By October 2026 the OpenHands/OpenHands repo holds 'Agent Canvas', a self-hosted web control centre that runs the OpenHands agent (from the MIT software-agent-sdk) or any ACP agent such as Claude Code or Codex; the old Python app moved to the archived OpenHands/legacy repo and the separate OpenHands CLI is marked no longer maintained.

facts.pricing: Free self-hosted (bring your own key); OpenHands Cloud individual tier free with BYOK or at-cost LLM usage; Enterprise custom
open_questions: Category is a judgement call: Agent Canvas is a self-hosted web app that runs sandboxed coding agents locally, on servers or on OpenHands Cloud; 'cloud-agent' chosen, could arguably be 'general-agent'.

Telemetry: PostHog analytics are consent-gated (opt-in), but the developer guide says one 'canvas_install' event fires pre-consent with an anonymous ID; Docker/npm builds ship a default PostHog key (VITE_DO_NOT_TRACK=1 disables).

Adoption: pypi openhands-ai is now the legacy package (last release 1.11.0, 2026-07-09); the live install path is npm @openhands/agent-canvas (created 2026-05-11) plus uvx openhands-agent-server. Consider switching the pypi counter to openhands-agent-server or dropping it.
Vendor: website copyright says 'OpenHands'; the 2026 enterprise LICENSE still names 'All Hands AI' as copyright holder. Unclear whether the company formally renamed.
Launch date is repo creation (2024-03-13, OpenDevin); first PyPI release openhands-ai 0.8.3 was 2024-08-20.

harnesses.dl_note: npm Agent Canvas + legacy PyPI app

harnesses.name: Goose
harnesses.vendor: Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); created by Block
harnesses.pricing: Free; bring your own API key, or use existing Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini subscriptions via ACP
harnesses.notes: Announced by Block as 'codename goose' in January 2025; the project now sits in the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation and the repo moved from block/goose to aaif-goose/goose. General-purpose agent (not only coding) with a desktop app, CLI and API, extended through MCP.

facts.pricing: Free; bring your own API key, or use existing Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini subscriptions via ACP
open_questions: GitHub has releases back to v0.9.0 (2024-09-10) from the earlier Python version of goose; 2025-01-28 is the official public announcement. Pick whichever convention the site uses.
Exact date goose was transferred to the Agentic AI Foundation not verified from a primary source here.

harnesses.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
harnesses.pricing: Free tier; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams usage-based (min $80/mo); Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Cognition renamed the Windsurf editor to Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02 (windsurf.com now redirects to devin.ai/desktop) and replaced its Cascade agent with 'Devin Local', the Devin CLI harness. The Windsurf/Codeium VS Code extension (Codeium.codeium) has been removed from the VS Code Marketplace; JetBrains plugins remain in maintenance.

facts.pricing: Free tier; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams usage-based (min $80/mo); Enterprise custom
open_questions: source/license 'Proprietary' inferred: no public repo or licence found; no explicit primary statement located, so sources are null.
Entry merges two products: Devin cloud agent (announced 2024-03, GA 2024-12) and Devin Desktop (Windsurf Editor, launched 2024-11). Launch uses the editor; split into two entries if needed.
Category: chose 'ide' (Devin Desktop); 'cloud-agent' fits the original Devin.
BYOK and local models not documented on current pages (Windsurf once allowed BYOK for some Claude models).
Telemetry: docs say code-snippet telemetry can be opted out in account settings; default implied on, not stated.

No live adoption identifier: Codeium.codeium returns 404 on the VS Code Marketplace (flagged unpublished, ~3.98M historical installs); Open VSX copy last updated 2025-06-16. devin.ai pricing page returned 404 to our User-Agent, so prices come from Cognition's April 2026 blog.

harnesses.name: Factory Droid
harnesses.pricing: Subscription (Pro $20/mo, Plus $100/mo, Max $200/mo; Teams/Business/Enterprise); bring-your-own-key custom models supported
harnesses.notes: Closed-source agent (npm package is UNLICENSED; the public Factory-AI/factory repo holds only a README and docs). Hosts frontier models from several labs and also accepts your own OpenAI/Anthropic keys or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including Ollama and LM Studio on localhost; site and docs moved from factory.ai to factory.com.

facts.pricing: Subscription (Pro $20/mo, Plus $100/mo, Max $200/mo; Teams/Business/Enterprise); bring-your-own-key custom models supported
open_questions: Launch: npm @factory/cli 0.1.0 was published 2025-08-07; Factory announced the full release of Droids (any model, any interface) on 2025-09-25 (https://siliconangle.com/2025/09/25/factory-unleashes-droids-software-agents-50m-fresh-funding/). Our old value 2025-09-25 is the GA date.

Telemetry: no docs page states the default. The CLI changelog (v0.238.0, 2026-10-10) says turning telemetry off 'now stops every Factory-bound log, trace, and metric', which implies it is on by default with an off switch; the setting name was not found.
Pricing page shows no free tier; unclear whether BYOK-only use requires a paid plan or just a Factory login.
npm package 'droid' (same maintainers, same description) is a second install name; package was originally registered in 2013 and appears to have been taken over by Factory. Not counted in adoption.

harnesses.name: Amp
harnesses.vendor: Amp Frontier Corporation (spun out of Sourcegraph)
harnesses.pricing: Free with your own model subscriptions/keys (BYOK, ChatGPT or Claude plans); Individual $20/mo includes remote 'orb' time; inference via Amp at cost; Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Amp announced on 2025-12-02 that it was spinning out of Sourcegraph as Amp Frontier Corporation, and it shut down its VS Code/editor extensions on 2026-03-05 to focus on the CLI, web and macOS/iOS apps. The npm package moved from @sourcegraph/amp to @ampcode/cli in May 2026; the bundled LICENSE.md still says 'Sourcegraph Inc. All rights reserved'.

facts.pricing: Free with your own model subscriptions/keys (BYOK, ChatGPT or Claude plans); Individual $20/mo includes remote 'orb' time; inference via Amp at cost; Enterprise custom
open_questions: Legal owner unclear: Amp says it became 'Amp Frontier Corporation', but the CLI licence still names Sourcegraph Inc.
local_models: BYOK list includes 'custom endpoint URLs' and Ollama Cloud, but running against a local Ollama/LM Studio server is not documented.
Telemetry not documented in the manual.
Legacy npm @sourcegraph/amp still publishes the same version (~17k/week vs ~23.5k/week for @ampcode/cli); sum both for adoption. sourcegraph.amp VS Code extension now 404 (removed).
Launch = general availability (waitlist removed) 2025-05-15; earlier private preview from ~April 2025.

harnesses.name: Crush
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional Charm Hyper subscription provider (free tier)
harnesses.notes: Not OSI open source: licensed FSL-1.1-MIT (Functional Source License, each version converts to MIT after two years) since 2025-07-28; the code it grew out of (Kujtim Hoxha's opencode, before Charm took it over) was MIT. Model list comes from Charm's open Catwalk database, and Charm sells its own 'Hyper' inference provider.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional Charm Hyper subscription provider (free tier)
open_questions: Our old record says open_source: true; under the brief's vocabulary FSL is source-available, not open source.
Launch: npm package created 2025-07-29 and earliest surviving GitHub release v0.1.6 is 2025-07-29; old record said 2025-07-30.

harnesses.name: Qwen Code
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key; or Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan subscription (free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15)
harnesses.notes: Forked from Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2; independent development since v0.1. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen API protocols plus local Ollama/vLLM; the free Qwen OAuth tier was discontinued on 2026-04-15.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key; or Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan subscription (free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15)
open_questions: npm package metadata has no license field (repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0).
Telemetry: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled defaults to true; the ToS doc says no extra data is collected for plain API-key users, so actual behaviour depends on auth method.

harnesses.name: Kimi Code
harnesses.pricing: Kimi Code Plan subscription or Moonshot API key; other providers with your own key
harnesses.notes: TypeScript rewrite that replaced the Python Kimi CLI (MoonshotAI/kimi-cli, Apache-2.0, now archived). Defaults to Kimi models but supports Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI Responses, Gemini and Vertex provider types.

facts.pricing: Kimi Code Plan subscription or Moonshot API key; other providers with your own key
open_questions: Local models: the openai provider type accepts any base_url, but the docs do not explicitly document Ollama/localhost use.
Plan prices: kimi.com/membership/pricing is JS-rendered and could not be read.
The VS Code extension moonshot-ai.kimi-code (first published 2026-01-23, before this repo existed) is listed as Apache-2.0 on Open VSX while the CLI repo is MIT.
Web UI ('kimi web') is documented in the command reference; the desktop app is from kimi.com/code, not the repo.

harnesses.name: Mistral Vibe
harnesses.pricing: Mistral API key (pay per token), or Vibe plans: limited Free, Pro $14.99/mo, Team $24.99/user/mo
harnesses.notes: Python CLI agent defaulting to Mistral Medium 3.5; it ships a default llama.cpp localhost provider and has Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and Vertex backends. Mistral now brands its whole assistant 'Vibe' (Le Chat became 'Vibe for work'); this entry is the CLI coding agent.

facts.pricing: Mistral API key (pay per token), or Vibe plans: limited Free, Pro $14.99/mo, Team $24.99/user/mo
open_questions: models/local_models come from source code (default providers include llamacpp at 127.0.0.1:8080; backends for anthropic, generic OpenAI-compatible, vertex); the README itself only documents Mistral API keys.
Launch: PyPI has a 0.0.0 placeholder from 2025-11-17; 1.0.0 and the first GitHub release are 2025-12-09.
Open VSX lists the VS Code extension licence as 'SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md' (not checked).

harnesses.name: Grok Build
harnesses.pricing: SuperGrok / X Premium+ subscription, or xAI API key
harnesses.notes: Rust terminal agent; source published under Apache-2.0 on 2026-07-14, synced from SpaceXAI's internal monorepo, and outside contributions are not accepted.

facts.pricing: SuperGrok / X Premium+ subscription, or xAI API key
open_questions: x.ai/cli and x.ai/build/changelog return HTTP 403 to fetchers, so the launch date (early beta 2026-05-14 for SuperGrok Heavy; public beta ~2026-05-25; v1.0 2026-08-07) and subscription tiers come from press, not primary sources.

Telemetry default: the config reference says 'Enterprise default is off', implying on for consumer builds; source builds without baked-in sinks send nothing. Disable with [features] telemetry or GROK_TELEMETRY_ENABLED.
Not distributed via npm (the old @vibe-kit/grok-cli is an unrelated community tool); GitHub has no releases, binaries come from x.ai/cli.
IDE use is via ACP only; no first-party VS Code extension found (several third-party ones exist).

harnesses.name: Warp
harnesses.pricing: Free plan with limited AI; Build $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Business $50/user/mo, Enterprise custom; bring-your-own-key for OpenAI/Anthropic/Google
harnesses.notes: Client open-sourced on 2026-04-28: app under AGPL-3.0-only, UI framework crates under MIT, with OpenAI as founding sponsor. The server, Warp Drive backend and Oz agent orchestration stay proprietary, and the built-in agent harness runs server-side, so the open repo is the terminal/editor client, not the agent itself.

facts.pricing: Free plan with limited AI; Build $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Business $50/user/mo, Enterprise custom; bring-your-own-key for OpenAI/Anthropic/Google
open_questions: Open-source date taken from the commit 'Initial public release of Warp' adding LICENSE-AGPL (2026-04-28). The repo itself dates from 2021 (it was the public issue tracker).

Models: Warp's hosted set comes from several labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, z.ai and others), plus BYOK for OpenAI/Anthropic/Google and 'custom inference endpoints' (OpenAI-compatible) on some plans; labelled 'curated', but could be 'any' if custom endpoints are open to individuals. The FAQ says you cannot use Claude/Codex subscriptions today; ACP support is on the roadmap.
Local models: not documented. Because the agent harness runs server-side, a localhost endpoint probably cannot work, but this is unconfirmed, so left null.
Telemetry nuance: on the Free plan telemetry must stay enabled to use AI features; paid plans can opt out; Business/Enterprise get zero data retention.
Category: Warp is its own desktop app (terminal plus editor plus agent). 'ide' chosen as closest; no 'terminal' category exists.
Launch: public beta 2022-04-05 (macOS). Our old value 2025-06-24 is the Warp 2.0 'agentic development environment' relaunch. Pick a convention.
Warp ships binaries from its own CDN; GitHub releases have no assets, so download counts can't be measured there.

harnesses.name: Roo Code
harnesses.pricing: Was free, bring your own key; Roo Code Cloud and Router shut down 2026-05-15
harnesses.notes: Fork of Cline (originally 'Roo Cline'). The team announced on 2026-04-20 that it was sunsetting the extension, Cloud and Router on 2026-05-15 to focus on the cloud agent Roomote. The repo was archived that day (last release 3.54.0), and roocode.com now redirects to roomote.dev. Installed copies still work but get no updates; the community continues the code as Zoo Code.

facts.pricing: Was free, bring your own key; Roo Code Cloud and Router shut down 2026-05-15
open_questions: Status: repo archived (2026-05-15) AND product officially sunset. I chose 'discontinued'; 'archived' would also be accurate.
website roocode.com now 301-redirects to roomote.dev.
The 3.53.0 changelog mentions an 'official handoff' to a community team, but the sunset post recommends only Cline. I found no primary Roo source naming Zoo Code as the official successor.
npm package 'roo-cline' (ISC, 2025-12, no repo link) is NOT Roo Code's; excluded from adoption.

harnesses.name: Aider
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key
harnesses.notes: Terminal pair-programming tool that edits files and commits to git. Development has slowed: last PyPI release 0.86.2 on 2026-02-12 (last GitHub release v0.86.0, 2025-08-09) and last commit to main on 2026-05-22.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key
open_questions: Our old note 'Dormant: no release since Aug 2025' is wrong: PyPI 0.86.2 shipped 2026-02-12. Still slow; 'active' is generous. Consider a 'slow / low activity' note rather than 'dormant'.
Telemetry: docs call analytics opt-in, but the consent prompt's default answer is [Yes] and it is shown to users on first run.
Launch: GitHub repo created 2023-05-09; first PyPI release 0.5.0 on 2023-06-08. Our old value used the repo-creation date.
Aider also has an experimental browser UI (--browser) and an IDE 'watch files' mode; only 'cli' listed.

harnesses.name: DeepSeek Harness
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key (DeepSeek API or other providers)
harnesses.notes: Developer-preview, plugin-based harness ('everything is a plugin', built on Cordis) for coding, documents, research and scheduled jobs; it is mainly a local web UI plus desktop app, not a terminal TUI. By default it attaches session-log data to requests sent to DeepSeek's official API (session-log-deepseek.enabled: false turns this off).

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key (DeepSeek API or other providers)
open_questions: Repo shows ~250,000 stars two months after creation, which is unusually high; worth checking before publishing star counts.
Launch: npm @deepseek-ai/dsh first published (rc) 2026-08-10, repo created 2026-08-13, first GitHub release 2026-08-17; 2026-08-13 used.
Telemetry is layered: Desktop product analytics default on with no UI toggle (config only); session upload defaults to FEEDBACK_ONLY; DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED turns off OTLP session telemetry.
local_models: docs say a custom provider can be 'a self-hosted server' (OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible); Ollama is not named.
Category could be argued as cli-agent; the official page markets it for documents, research and automation as well as coding.
No official VS Code extension; several third-party ones exist.

harnesses.name: Zoo Code
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional credits for Zoo Gateway and cloud agents, optional Team plan
harnesses.notes: Community continuation of Roo Code by former Roo contributors after Roo was sunset. The repo carries Roo's full git history and is not a GitHub-network fork. It keeps the same features, settings structure and Apache-2.0 licence, and has added features since (v3.88 on GitHub and about 105k VS Code Marketplace installs as of 2026-10-15).

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key; optional credits for Zoo Gateway and cloud agents, optional Team plan
open_questions: No legal entity identified: the LICENSE says 'Copyright 2026 Zoo Code' and the website says it is community-maintained, yet it sells credits and a Team plan. Who operates billing is unclear.
Website mentions a JetBrains plugin in beta; not verified on JetBrains Marketplace, so it was not added to interfaces.
Launch = Marketplace first publish 2026-05-08 (GitHub repo created 2026-04-23; first GitHub release v3.54.0 on 2026-05-16).

harnesses.name: Letta Code
harnesses.pricing: Free tier (3 stateful agents, BYOK); Pro $20/mo; API plan $20/mo plus usage; Teams $20/seat/mo; Enterprise custom
harnesses.notes: Letta Code is a harness: an Apache-2.0 terminal/desktop agent ('stateful agent harness') with persistent memory that rewrites its own memory, skills and prompts, and can also be reached from Slack, Telegram, Discord and chat.letta.com. It is separate from the Letta platform (letta-ai/letta, formerly MemGPT), which is a server/framework for building stateful agents and should not be listed as a harness.

facts.pricing: Free tier (3 stateful agents, BYOK); Pro $20/mo; API plan $20/mo plus usage; Teams $20/seat/mo; Enterprise custom
open_questions: Category: began as a memory-first coding agent, now pitched as a general stateful agent harness ('more like people than tools'); 'general-agent' chosen, 'cli-agent' also defensible.

Local models: Ollama ('Ollama (local)', http://localhost:11434/v1) and LM Studio providers ship in the source, and the CLI offers a local backend, but no docs page explicitly documents a fully local setup. Letta Cloud is the default backend.

Telemetry: code says 'Enabled by default unless explicitly disabled', with opt-out via LETTA_CODE_TELEM or DO_NOT_TRACK=1; not confirmed in user docs, and unclear whether it applies when using the local backend.
Name: suggest the entry be named 'Letta Code' rather than 'Letta', since the Letta platform/server is a framework.

harnesses.name: ZCode
harnesses.pricing: Free app; GLM Coding Plan subscription (free Start Plan quota) or your own API key
harnesses.notes: Z.ai's official harness for its GLM models: a desktop app, browser UI and terminal agent sharing one TypeScript runtime. Launched closed, open-sourced under Apache-2.0 in September 2026.

facts.pricing: Free app; GLM Coding Plan subscription (free Start Plan quota) or your own API key
open_questions: Launch date 2026-07-01 is from press; zcode.z.ai shows no date. Repo created 2026-09-20; first GitHub release v3.14.3 on 2026-09-24.
Telemetry: the source posts events to zcode.z.ai/api/v1/event/report and Alibaba ARMS monitoring; no documented user opt-out found, so left null.
Category: primarily a desktop app with no code editor ('agentic development environment'); recorded as cli-agent because it also ships a TUI agent. Reconsider.
local_models: custom OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible providers are supported, but localhost/Ollama use is not documented.
The workspace-upload report comes from secondary sources (press, a user's reverse-engineering report); check before publishing.

harnesses.name: Muse Code
harnesses.pricing: Meta Model API pay-as-you-go (cheaper 'contributor' rates if Meta may use your data) or subscription $5-$200/mo
harnesses.notes: Publicly available. Meta's terminal multi-agent coding agent, built for its Muse Spark models and installed with a curl script; it launched in beta on 2026-08-05 and is now out of beta. The agent is closed source; only its session-protocol SDK (meta-models/muse-code-sdk) is MIT.

facts.pricing: Meta Model API pay-as-you-go (cheaper 'contributor' rates if Meta may use your data) or subscription $5-$200/mo
open_questions: Models: docs mention 'other providers' and a --provider flag (changelog 1.4.2) but document only Meta credentials; it is unclear whether non-Meta or local models are supported, so left null.
Telemetry: the configuration docs say the settings file holds 'telemetry options' but give no defaults.
Licence 'Proprietary' rests on there being no public source repo and no licence statement; the binary comes from api.meta.ai.
Platforms: the launch blog says macOS and Linux; the product page now says macOS and Windows.
No measurable adoption identifier for the agent itself; the SDK is npm @muse-code/sdk / repo meta-models/muse-code-sdk (61 stars).

harnesses.name: VSCodium
harnesses.pricing: Free
harnesses.notes: No AI of its own: models come through the agents it hosts from Open VSX (Cline, Kilo Code, Continue, Zoo Code).

facts.pricing: Free
open_questions: launch is the date of the 1.26.0 tag commit (2018-08-15); the matching GitHub release may have gone up a day or two later

Copilot can apparently still be sideloaded by hand: VSCodium docs explain how to re-enable it with a custom product.json, and product.json still enables Copilot API proposals. Whether that is allowed under GitHub's and Microsoft's terms is not settled here
models/local_models are null on purpose: VSCodium has no AI of its own, so these depend on the extension installed

harnesses.name: LM Studio
harnesses.pricing: Free app (incl. work use since 2025-07-08); optional cloud plans Bionic+ $20/mo, Pro $100/mo
harnesses.notes: The desktop app is closed source; GitHub stars count only its open-source lms command-line tool.

facts.pricing: Free app (incl. work use since 2025-07-08); optional cloud plans Bionic+ $20/mo, Pro $100/mo
open_questions: launch is the first Wayback capture of lmstudio.ai (2023-05-24); I found no official release note giving the date
the privacy policy says 'no telemetry', but update checks and anonymised model-search queries are still sent, and there is no documented switch to turn them off
lms has no GitHub release assets (it ships inside the app), so it gives no download counts. Stars are the only GitHub signal
npm package 'lmstudio' (Apache-2.0, a setup tool) is a separate official package; I left it out of adoption

harnesses.repo_note: stars of its open-source lms CLI only
harnesses.dl_note: its developer SDK (npm + PyPI), not the app

harnesses.name: AnythingLLM
harnesses.pricing: Free (desktop and self-hosted Docker); paid hosted Cloud
harnesses.notes: An all-in-one chat-with-documents (RAG) and agent app for desktop or self-hosted Docker, with multi-user support, MCP and a no-code agent builder. It is a general AI workspace rather than a coding harness. Telemetry goes to PostHog and is switched off with DISABLE_TELEMETRY or a Privacy toggle in the app.

facts.pricing: Free (desktop and self-hosted Docker); paid hosted Cloud
open_questions: launch is the date the GitHub repo was created (2023-06-04); I found no separate release date
prices for the hosted Cloud plans are not on anythingllm.com
the desktop installers come from anythingllm.com. I did not confirm they are built only from the MIT repo, or what the GitHub release assets are (about 573k downloads in total)

harnesses.name: Freebuff
harnesses.pricing: Free, ad-supported, with daily session limits; paid plans unlock more models
harnesses.notes: Free because ad-funded: its privacy policy uses prompts and project data to target ads. No telemetry opt-out is documented.

facts.pricing: Free, ad-supported, with daily session limits; paid plans unlock more models
open_questions: the repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0 ('Copyright 2025 Freebuff, Inc.') but the npm package 'freebuff' says MIT

the github.com/CodebuffAI/codebuff URL now redirects to CodebuffAI/freebuff, so Codebuff and Freebuff share one repo. Codebuff's own npm package (codebuff, first published 2024-11-04) is still being released
telemetry 'on, cannot disable' is my inference: the privacy policy describes no opt-out for CLI/desktop analytics, and cli/src/utils/analytics.ts (PostHog) has no user switch. Not stated outright
local_models false means the README lists only the hosted catalogue. Freebuff Desktop can drive a locally installed Claude Code or Codex, but those use their own provider accounts, not local models
launch is the date the 'freebuff' npm package was created; I did not find a launch announcement
prices for the paid plans were not on the homepage

the GitHub release assets are beta CLI binaries named 'codecane-*' (e.g. v1.0.420-beta.185). The npm package and desktop installers are probably the main channels, so release download counts will understate use

harnesses.name: omp (oh-my-pi)
harnesses.pricing: Free; bring your own key or sign in with an existing provider subscription
harnesses.notes: A fork of Mario Zechner's Pi coding agent (badlogic/pi-mono) by Can Bölük, now maintained by Stencil Labs, with a Rust core and LSP/debugger (DAP) tools built into the terminal agent. It supports 60+ providers, including Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM.

facts.pricing: Free; bring your own key or sign in with an existing provider subscription
open_questions: telemetry 'none' comes from reading the code: I found no vendor analytics SDK, and the only telemetry setting (telemetry.otlpExportEnabled, default on) exports OpenTelemetry to OTEL_* endpoints the user configures. No privacy statement says this
launch is the date the npm package was created; the fork may have been public on GitHub a little earlier
the npm package 'omp' is unrelated (2019, ISC); do not use it
the site advertises a coming 'omp²'

harnesses.name: Zed
harnesses.pricing: Free with own API keys or external agents; Pro $10/mo; Business $30/seat/mo
harnesses.notes: A native editor written in Rust with its own agent panel and edit predictions. Through the Agent Client Protocol it also hosts external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex. It went open source on 2024-01-24 and reached 1.0 on 2026-04-29.

facts.pricing: Free with own API keys or external agents; Pro $10/mo; Business $30/seat/mo
open_questions: GitHub shows the licence as NOASSERTION because the repo holds LICENSE-GPL and LICENSE-APACHE. The README says the code is 'primarily GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components'. The LICENSE-AGPL file that used to cover the collab server now returns 404
launch is the public beta (2023-03-15, macOS only); there was an invite-only alpha in 2022

harnesses.name: Continue
harnesses.pricing: Free, bring your own key (no longer maintained)
harnesses.notes: Cursor acquired Continue in June 2026. The homepage now shows only the acquisition notice, and the README says the repo is read-only and no longer maintained. The final 2.x release of the VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin and CLI removed telemetry and authentication, so the code still runs with your own keys or local models.

facts.pricing: Free, bring your own key (no longer maintained)
open_questions: exact acquisition date: continue.dev gives none; press reports put the announcement around 2026-06-16 to 06-22. The last GitHub release (v2.1.0-vscode) is dated 2026-06-19
the README says the repo is read-only, but the GitHub API reports archived=false
the status vocabulary allows one value. 'acquired:Cursor' is used, though the product is effectively discontinued
launch is the first VS Code Marketplace publish (2023-05-27); the repo was created 2023-05-24
PyPI 'continuedev' (Apache-2.0, 2023) is the old Python server and stale; I left it out of adoption

harnesses.name: CodeGPT
harnesses.pricing: Free tier (10 daily interactions, unlimited BYOK); Professional $10/mo; Teams $30/user/mo
harnesses.notes: A closed-source VS Code and JetBrains coding-agent extension. You can bring your own keys, use local models through Ollama or LM Studio, or buy CodeGPT credits. The company also sells business AI agents through a web platform and API; the public GitHub repo (JudiniLabs/code-gpt-docs) holds only documentation.

facts.pricing: Free tier (10 daily interactions, unlimited BYOK); Professional $10/mo; Teams $30/user/mo
open_questions: telemetry is null: the privacy policy (v1.2, 2025-03-04) says it collects usage data (prompt counts, time used, tokens, VS Code user/device IDs) but names no opt-out apart from contacting support
licence is 'Proprietary' from the Open VSX metadata; I found no LICENSE file, because the only public repo is documentation
npm 'codegpt' and PyPI 'codegpt' are unrelated third-party projects; do not map them
launch is the first VS Code Marketplace publish (2022-12-25)
